chapter: Small groups, Europe and Kansas City memories (repeated passages)
title: The Subway jam sessions and Piney Brown in Kansas City
summary: Musicians jammed at the Subway, run by Piney Brown; Kansas City was a jumping bootleg town in the depression, where he met Jack Teagarden.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: It was a jam; you know, it was a jam. We used to go to a place down in Kansas City and jam. You know? Called the Subway. It was on 18th and Vine, and it was under a place...under a restaurant called Eleanor's -- and she had very good food there. And it was under there, a basement down in there called the Subway. And the guys used to go down there and jam. And the guy that ran it was named Piney Brown. I don't know if you've ever heard that name...
Yeah, because of "Piney Brown's Blues". Joe Turner made a record...
I guess he was a good friend to a lot of musicians, too.
Yeah, he was a nice man.

Oh, it was a jumpin' town in them days. Those were bootlegging days, but they were good days. I don't mean they were... I didn't make a whole lot of money or anything, but... Because the Depression was on yet, you know...
That was in the middle of the Depression, you know. But we had fun with what we had.
[What? I didn't even see him hit the ball.]
Well, you see, that's... I met Jack Teagarden down there. He used to come down there and jam.

Yeah. I was staying a hotel there, and any time anybody was having any jams, the guys would come up to the hotel and call me...or call me, and say, "Come on down, man, the guys is blowin'!" You know? So I would go down.
